title: Kente Cloth and the Architecture of Akan Identity
creator: Asante Weavers, Bonwire
summary: Kente is not merely decorative cloth. Each named pattern encodes cosmology, genealogy, and social ethics — a visual text within the Akan world.

title: The Wretched of the Earth
creator: Frantz Fanon
summary: Fanon's foundational text on the psychology and politics of colonialism and decolonisation. Indispensable to decolonial thought.

title: Decolonising Design in Africa
creator: Yaw Ofosu-Asare
summary: Maps the epistemological stakes of design education across the African continent through Sankofa methodology and decolonial critique.

title: African Design Futures
creator: Yaw Ofosu-Asare
summary: A programmatic framework for reimagining African design practice, pedagogy, and spatial production beyond colonial inheritance.

title: Yoruba Ifa Oral Corpus
creator: Yoruba Babalawo tradition
summary: One of the world's most extensive oral knowledge archives — a comprehensive cosmological, philosophical, and ethical system transmitted through Babalawo lineages.

title: Benin Bronzes: A Documentation Record
creator: Edo craftspeople, Benin City
summary: Among the most technically sophisticated metal artworks ever produced. Looted by British forces in 1897, thousands remain scattered across European and North American institutions.
provenance: Looted by British Punitive Expedition, 1897. British Museum (900+), Ethnologisches Museum Berlin, and others.

title: Great Zimbabwe: Architectural Documentation
creator: Shona builders (Kingdom of Zimbabwe)
summary: The largest precolonial stone structure in sub-Saharan Africa. Colonial authorities suppressed its African origin. Its recovery as a symbol of African civilisation is central to Zimbabwean identity.

title: Consciencism: Philosophy and Ideology for De-colonization
creator: Kwame Nkrumah
summary: Nkrumah's philosophical framework synthesising African communalist tradition, Islam, and Euro-Christian inheritance into a foundation for African socialist politics.

title: Mau Mau Testimonies: Oral Archive
creator: Kenya Human Rights Commission / Kenya National Archives
summary: Testimonies from survivors of British colonial detention camps during the Mau Mau uprising — accounts documentary records were designed to erase.
provenance: Kenya National Archives / KHRC oral testimony collections.

title: Anti-Apartheid Movement Poster Archive
creator: ANC, PAC, UDF, COSATU
summary: Political posters produced by South African liberation movements — a significant archive of decolonial visual culture produced under censorship.
provenance: South African National Gallery, SOAS Digital Collections, and community archives.

title: Timbuktu Manuscripts: West African Islamic Scholarship
creator: Various Malian and West African scholars
summary: Approximately 400,000 manuscripts document West African mathematics, astronomy, medicine, jurisprudence, and philosophy — a counter-archive to colonial narratives of a pre-literate Africa.
provenance: Ahmed Baba Institute, Timbuktu. Some digitised via Hamburg University.

title: Ndebele Wall Painting: Visual Knowledge Traditions
creator: Ndebele women artists, Mpumalanga
summary: A visual language developed and transmitted by women. Geometric patterns encode social status, identity, and cosmological knowledge — intensified as cultural resistance during apartheid.

title: Return to the Source: Selected Speeches of Amilcar Cabral
creator: Amilcar Cabral
summary: Cabral's speeches articulate culture as a force of liberation — culture as the foundation of political freedom and the site of decolonisation.

title: Ubuntu Philosophy: A Communal Ethics
creator: Various African philosophy scholars
summary: Ubuntu — 'I am because we are' — frames communal personhood, ethical reciprocity, and shared humanity across much of sub-Saharan African social thought.

title: Lamu Old Town: Swahili Coast Architecture
creator: Swahili master builders
summary: The oldest and best-preserved Swahili settlement in East Africa demonstrates an urban tradition shaped through Indian Ocean trade networks long before European colonialism.
provenance: Lamu County, Kenya. UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2001.

title: Sankofa Methodology in Design Education
creator: Yaw Ofosu-Asare
summary: Sankofa — 'it is not wrong to go back for what you forgot' — is used here as a methodological framework for recovering precolonial knowledge architectures as generative design tools.

title: Dialogues of Liberation: Fanon, Cabral, and Nkrumah
creator: Yaw Ofosu-Asare
summary: Comparative reading of Fanon, Cabral, and Nkrumah as a unified philosophical project — tracing convergences in their theories of culture, consciousness, and political transformation.

title: PRAAD: Public Records and Archives Administration
creator: Government of Ghana
summary: The national repository for Ghana's public records includes colonial administrative documents, treaties, maps, photographs, and land records from the Gold Coast era onward.
provenance: Public Records and Archives Administration Department, Accra, Ghana.

title: Adinkra Symbols: A Visual Philosophy of the Akan
creator: Akan artisans, Ashanti Region
summary: Adinkra symbols encode proverbs, philosophical concepts, and historical events in visual form — a system of pictographic communication used in textiles, pottery, metalwork, and architecture.
provenance: Ntonso and surrounding communities, Ashanti Region, Ghana.

title: Steve Biko: I Write What I Like
creator: Steve Biko
summary: Collected writings of Steve Biko — the foundational text of Black Consciousness philosophy in South Africa, arguing for psychological decolonisation as the precondition for liberation.
